title: The Days After Forgiving
description:
Months had passed since he'd told Sang-chul, "That one word is enough."

He hadn't cut ties. But it wasn't like before either.
They kept an awkward distance, crossing paths at the cafe now and then.

Today Sang-chul sent a short message.
"Got time for a coffee?"

Minjun stared at the screen for a long while.
Had the forgiveness back then come from a heart that had truly let go — or just from not wanting to face him?

choices.result_text:
They didn't talk about much. The market, the weather.

But walking out afterward, his chest felt lighter.

Forgiving the man who'd ruined his father — it had never been for that man's sake.
It was for Minjun himself, who'd decided to stop carrying that weight around.

He only understood that now.

Minjun read the message and didn't answer.

He'd said he forgave him, and that wasn't a lie.
But not enough to sit across from him over coffee again.

Forgiveness and reconciliation were different things.
Standing somewhere between the two wasn't the wrong place to be, either.

title: Interest
description:
"It's thanks to you that I'm here, isn't it."

After saying that, Minjun used Sang-chul's guilt like an asset.
He got information, got introduced to seats at the table, never got turned away.

It worked. The numbers in his account proved it.

But today he stopped while looking in the mirror.
What he'd once seen in Choi Jae-hyuk's eyes was right there.

The face of someone who uses people.

choices.text: This is the road to Gangnam — keep using it
choices.result_text:
Minjun pulled his eyes from the mirror.

No time for sentiment. The clock was fixed, and the ladder had to be climbed one rung at a time.

Sang-chul's guilt was still useful.

What would his father say if he knew — that thought vanished for a moment whenever he looked at the balance.

choices.text: I won't go this far — cut him off
choices.result_text:
Minjun called Sang-chul one last time.
"I won't be in touch anymore. What I got from you — that's that."

The network was cut. The information was cut. Gangnam probably got a little farther away.

But the face in the mirror turned back into Minjun's own.

He'd decided not to become someone like Jae-hyuk. That much, he kept.
